### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, every trace contained the consecutive block A22 → A23 → A24: all of A22's outgoing transitions went to A23, all of A23's went to A24, and A24 followed A22 exactly two steps later in all 200 traces. [DIR004, DIR005, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003]
- In the later window, three activities that appear in none of the 200 earlier traces — A14, A15 and A20 — now occur once each in about 29, 41 and 30 in 100 traces (58, 82 and 59 of 200), never twice in the same trace, and sit near the middle of the trace (mean relative position about 0.51 for all three). [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, POS001, POS002, POS003]
- In the later window the new activities interrupt the old block: about 56 in 100 of A22's outgoing transitions now go to A14, A15 or A20 (before, all went to A23), and about 44 in 100 of A23's outgoing transitions go to A14, A15 or A20 (before, all went to A24). [DIR004, DIR005]
- The new activities themselves lead to A23 in about 53–58 in 100 of their outgoing transitions and to A24 in about 42–47 in 100. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003]
- Step distances shifted accordingly: A22→A23 is now two steps apart in about 56 in 100 cases (before always one), A23→A24 two steps in about 44 in 100 (before always one), and A22→A24 three steps in virtually every later trace (before always two). [LAG001, LAG002, LAG003]
- A22 now occurs slightly earlier within traces (mean relative position about 0.48 before versus about 0.46 after). [POS004]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that, in the later window, exactly one of the previously unobserved activities A14, A15 or A20 is inserted into the formerly fixed sequence A22 → A23 → A24 — between A22 and A23 in roughly 56 in 100 traces and between A23 and A24 in the remaining roughly 44 in 100. [DIR004, DIR005, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003] The single-insertion reading fits the data closely: the three participations sum to about 100 in 100 traces, no activity repeats within a trace, and the A22→A24 distance is three steps in virtually all later traces, which is what one inserted step produces. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, LAG002] The pattern is direct and internally consistent — 15 qualifying evidence items against roughly 0.34 expected by chance in the control-flow family — and a rare-variant explanation is implausible because none of 200 earlier traces contains any of the three activities while 58–82 of 200 later traces do. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003] Limitations: the evidence cannot show what determines which of the three activities is inserted or at which of the two positions, and the exact split (about 56/44) comes from a single sample of 200 traces; a competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out is that the choice of activity and insertion point depends on case characteristics not visible here, with the data showing only the aggregate shares. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003]
